To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of Th1 and Th2 responses to Gag, Env, and Tat antigens correlates with vaccine-induced protection from SHIV infection.
immunization with multiple HIV antigens induces qualitatively different Th responses to individual antigens than immunization with a single antigen.

(1) the magnitude and quality of the vaccine-induced Th responses to the individual HIV antigens are important in predicting vaccine efficacy and that (2) a combination of antigens is superior to a single antigen in terms of vaccine efficacy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a vaccine to control HIV infection.
the development and evaluation of novel HIV vaccine candidates in the rhesus macaque model of HIV infection.
developing a vaccine that can prevent the spread of HIV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vaccine-induced immune responses were qualitatively different and that the qualitative responses were associated with vaccine efficacy.
the vaccine-induced Th immune responses are critical for vaccine efficacy and that the Th responses to multiple HIV antigens should be included in an HIV vaccine.
the Th1/Th2 paradigm is not as simplistic as previously thought, and that a Th2-biased response may not necessarily be detrimental to the host.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that immunization with multiple viral antigens induced a Th response that is more protective than immunization with a single viral antigen.
a combination of antigens is required for protection and the quality of the responses to individual antigens is also critical for protection.
a Th2 response to one antigen can be overcome by Th1-like responses to other antigens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Th responses are not only important for vaccine-induced immunity, but the type of Th response is critical.
vaccine-induced immunity to HIV requires a combination of strong Th1- and strong Th2-like responses.
vaccine-induced protection from disease is associated with a strong Th1/Th2 response to the Gag and Env structural proteins.
